findings.title: Representative fee described as additional to compensation

original_quote.text: out of any compensation benefits due
original_quote.anchor: C-3.0 (6-22), PDF page 4, Your Rights, point 6

translated_quote.text: además de los beneficios de compensación pagaderos
translated_quote.anchor: C-3.0 (6-22), PDF page 4, Sus derechos, point 6

findings.faithful_english: in addition to the compensation benefits payable
findings.difference: The English says the approved representative fee comes out of benefits due; the Spanish describes the fee as in addition to payable benefits. Both say the employer or insurer remits an approved fee and the worker should not pay the representative directly.
findings.confidence: Moderate translation confidence; low confidence in any legal-effect change
findings.same_facts_example: Illustration only: on a $10,000 award with a $1,500 approved fee, the English wording describes $8,500 remaining after deduction. A literal Spanish reading can suggest the worker retains $10,000 while the carrier separately pays $1,500. This is not a statutory fee calculation for a particular claim.
findings.counterargument: Both forms identify the employer or insurer as remitter, so the Spanish could describe a separate remittance rather than a separate economic source.
findings.response: The ordinary meaning of además de is in addition to, whereas out of identifies the award as the source. Current Board representation guidance says the fee is deducted from the award.
findings.potential_consequence: A claimant reading only Spanish could form a materially inaccurate expectation of the net award. The form cannot itself alter the governing fee rule.
findings.documented_consequence: No actual changed payment, claimant reliance, dispute, or translation-caused harm was established in the bounded official-source search.
findings.independent_review: Independent reviewer checked matched official four-page 6-22 PDFs, saved SHA-256 captures, rendered PDF page 4 images, aligned context, Board guidance, and a bounded official case-law search.
findings.authority_note: WCB claimant representation guidance says approved fees are deducted from awards. The 2026 Gonzalez decision describes the fee as a lien on the award; it did not decide a translation dispute.

authorities.label: Gonzalez v State of New York, 2026

findings.case_law_status: Bounded official-court search found no decision on Spanish C-3 wording or claimant reliance; Gonzalez concerns fee calculation, not translation.
findings.coverage_note: One aligned rights-instruction meaning unit within a four-page form; the project has not certified full-form review.
findings.current_relevance: The WCB forms index still linked both C-3.0 (6-22) editions when rechecked on 26 October 2026; the 2023 fee schedule affects any real-case calculation.

findings.title: Mailing label rendered as an envelope

original_quote.text: a self-sticking 4” wide and 1” high mailing label
original_quote.anchor: Fact Sheet #18 (11/2023), PDF page 1, Filing Requirements

translated_quote.text: un sobre postal con adhesivo, de 4 pulgadas de ancho por 1 pulgada de alto
translated_quote.anchor: Fact Sheet #18, Modificado (11/2023), PDF page 1, Requisitos de presentación

findings.faithful_english: an adhesive mailing envelope, 4 inches wide by 1 inch high
findings.difference: For an owner filing a Petition for Administrative Review affecting multiple tenants, English requests an addressed adhesive mailing label; Spanish requests an adhesive mailing envelope of the same dimensions.
findings.confidence: High confidence in the noun contrast; context may help readers infer the intended label
findings.same_facts_example: An owner preparing an otherwise complete multi-tenant appeal follows the Spanish sentence and supplies addressed envelopes rather than the 4-by-1-inch labels specified in the English fact sheet and RAR-2 instructions.
findings.counterargument: An envelope only one inch high is physically unusual, so the stated dimensions and address context may tell a careful reader that a label was intended.
findings.response: Sobre postal ordinarily means envelope, not label; the Spanish paragraph does not use etiqueta. The operative RAR-2 instructions confirm labels are requested.
findings.potential_consequence: Wrong stationery may trigger a correction request or delay service. The reviewed rules do not show that this specific error automatically forfeits an appeal.
findings.documented_consequence: No actual rejection, missed deadline, reliance, or translation-caused harm was established in the bounded official-source search.
findings.independent_review: Independent reviewer checked matching November 2023 three-page official PDFs, saved SHA-256 captures, rendered PDF page 1 images, RAR-2 instructions, bulletin 90-1r, and the sheet’s procedural-correction paragraph.
findings.authority_note: HCR says these English-origin translations are guidance that does not replace English originals. RAR-2 and Operational Bulletin 90-1r require labels for multi-tenant PARs; the fact sheet describes a correction route for procedural defects.
findings.case_law_status: Bounded official-source search found no decision tying this Spanish wording to loss of a PAR.
findings.coverage_note: One aligned filing-requirements meaning unit within a three-page fact sheet; the project has not certified full-sheet review.
findings.current_relevance: HCR’s translation directory still linked both November 2023 editions when rechecked on 26 October 2026.
